item.title: LIV Golf’s Iron Heads GC rebrands as Korean Golf Club
item.description: LIV Golf’s Iron Heads Golf Club will compete as Korean Golf Club for the 2026 season. The team unveiled a rebrand that reflects Korea’s growing influence on global golf culture and a reimagined vision for what modern golf can be. item.title: Koepka rejoins PGA Tour, accepts penalties
item.description: Brooks Koepka announced his return to the PGA Tour on Monday under new rules for LIV players.

item.title: Stinger GC rebrands as Southern Guards GC
item.description: LIV Golf's Stinger GC has rebranded as Southern Guards GC, marking a significant new chapter for South Africa’s team on the world stage.

item.title: LIV trio snub PGA Tour offer
item.description: Major winners Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith have all committed to stay with LIV Golf in 2026.

item.title: Johnson extends LIV Golf contract
item.description: 4Aces GC have secured the services of captain Dustin Johnson on a multi-year contract extension.

item.title: McIlroy takes lead at Dubai Invitational
item.description: Rory McIlroy made a strong start to the new year after carding a five-under par 66 to hold a one-shot lead following the 1st round of the Dubai Invitational on Thursday.

item.title: Taylor tied for lead at Sony Open
item.description: Defending champion Nick Taylor shared the first-round lead with Kevin Roy on Thursday in the PGA Tour's season-opening Sony Open in Hawaii.

item.title: Oosthuizen: LIV Golf bigger than any individual
item.description: Louis Oosthuizen has played down the significance of Brooks Koepka’s return to the PGA Tour from LIV Golf.

item.title: McIlroy slips off Dubai lead, Saffas in the hunt
item.description: Rory McIlroy endured a tricky second day at the Dubai Invitational on Friday as he posted a three-over round of 74 to slip off the top of the leaderboard. item.title: Five share Sony Open lead, Saffas miss cut
item.description: Defending champion Nick Taylor remained tied for the lead at the PGA Tour's Sony Open on Friday, but the Canadian had quite a bit more company at the top.
